access.edition_or_version: The Complete Essays of Montaigne, trans. Donald M. Frame (Stanford, 1958)

mechanics.premise: The self is put on trial as the instrument and object of inquiry; each essay tests a judgment without settling it.
mechanics.argumentative_stance: Provisional and open-ended; the essay is an 'attempt' whose value lies in the testing, not a verdict. Titles pose topics; digression is licensed.
mechanics.point_of_view: First-person essayistic 'I' used as evidence, but turned outward to general reflection rather than confessional interiority.
mechanics.structure: Associative, digressive movement among anecdotes, quotations and self-observation; no forced conclusion.
mechanics.style_and_devices: Concrete anecdote as entry point to principle; quotation as counterpoint; ordinary diction with occasional aphoristic compression.
mechanics.dialogue: Internal dialogue with ancient authors and with the reader's assumed objections rather than dramatised characters.
mechanics.imagery: Domestic and bodily images used to make abstract questions tractable.
mechanics.emotional_progression: Curiosity and doubt; equanimity rather than catharsis.
mechanics.critical_reception: Founding instance of the essay genre; widely treated as the origin of the modern personal essay and of essayistic scepticism.
mechanics.failure_or_misuse_signals: Digression without a governing idea; self-reference that never abstracts outward collapses into tone-reflective.
